headline: Trump invites Putin to G20 summit in Miami
summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says the invitation is an opportunity for the Russian leader to engage with world leaders as Washington seeks to end the Ukraine war.
details: President Donald Trump has invited Russian President Vladimir Putin to attend the G20 summit in Miami this December. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced the move following a meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov in New York.

Rubio stated that meeting with those one disagrees with is essential to solving problems. He expressed hope that Putin will accept the invitation to engage with both the US president and other world leaders.
The invitation comes as Washington attempts to secure a deal to end Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Trump has insisted he is working with both sides to stop the war.
Meanwhile, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told the UN Security Council that Moscow will not halt its 'special military operation' in Ukraine, accusing Europe of using any pause to arm Kyiv.
Rubio has also encouraged both Moscow and Kyiv to reach an energy ceasefire, noting that both sides have expressed interest in a limited agreement involving energy infrastructure.
Despite diplomatic efforts, violence continues on the ground. Russian strikes on civilian infrastructure across Ukraine killed at least seven people yesterday, including two in Kyiv.

Further casualties were reported in the Donbas region and Odesa, where a cargo ship captain was killed in a Russian attack. More than 40 people were wounded in strikes hitting gas stations, offices and rail networks.

headline: Fuel price hikes: Govt raises bus fares by Tk 0.17 per km after fuel jump
summary: The government has issued a gazette raising bus and minibus fares. This follows a steep climb in diesel prices, which jumped to Tk 135 per litre on September 21.
details: The Bangladesh government has officially raised bus and minibus fares by Tk 0.17 per km following a series of fuel price hikes. This move comes as diesel prices surged to Tk 135 per litre on September 21, after previously jumping to Tk 115 in April.

According to the energy ministry, international fuel prices more than doubled since March, and regional instability has caused freight charges to spike. This resulted in a staggering Tk 22,876 crore loss for the Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation (BPC) between March and August.

Officials state that the new pricing is intended to trim annual losses by approximately Tk 10,000 crore, save foreign reserves, and curb fuel smuggling to neighboring countries where prices are higher.

The article highlights that while most oil-importing nations in Asia, including Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and India, have had to raise fuel prices due to global market shocks, the approach differs. Some countries use transparent daily pricing or targeted subsidies for low-income households.

The author argues that Bangladesh's pricing mechanism is often discretionary rather than following the IMF-backed mechanism introduced in 20 24, which leads to unpredictability for businesses and commuters.
Ultimately, the fuel price increases are a ripple effect of global oil markets, as Bangladesh imports 95 percent of its oil and 30 percent of its oil-gas, meaning costs are passed on to the citizens.
caption:
Bus fares are going up. Diesel prices have surged to Tk 135 per litre, forcing a government-approved fare hike.

The Bangladesh government has officially raised bus and minibus fares by Tk 0.17 per km following a series of fuel price hikes. This move comes as diesel prices surged to Tk 135 per litre on September 21, after previously jumping to Tk 115 in April.

The author argues that Bangladesh's pricing mechanism is often discretionary rather than following the IMF-backed mechanism introduced in 20 24, which leads to unpredictability for businesses and commuters.
